UPSTREAM: cpufreq: Allow drivers to enable boost support after registering driver In some cases it wouldn't be known at time of driver registration, if the driver needs to support boost frequencies. For example, while getting boost information from DT with opp-v2 bindings, we need to parse the bindings for all the CPUs to know if turbo/boost OPPs are supported or not. One way out to do that efficiently is to delay supporting boost mode (i.e. creating /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/boost file), until the time OPP bindings are parsed. At that point, the driver can enable boost support. This can be done at ->init(), where the frequency table is created. To do that, the driver requires few APIs from cpufreq core that let him do this. This patch provides these APIs. libcontainer: Allow relative source when mounting externally Only mounts made inside minijail were checked for being relative to the runtime root. Allow mounts made outside to be relative as well. Thus, if a mount needs to be made externally, it can still be specified relative to the runtime root path of the container. This allows the bind mount of /dev/pts/ptmx to /dev/ptmx to be made outside and have its selinux context set correctly. BUG=none TEST=run container on minnie with root-relative, external mount. power: Support enabling keyboard backlight for user activity Add a new keyboard_backlight_turn_on_for_user_activity pref (on by default) that can be set to instruct powerd to keep the keyboard backlight off except when user activity (keyboard, touchpad) is observed. This can be set on systems that lack ambient light sensors and hover detection to reduce the keyboard backlight's power consumption. Also rename keyboard_backlight_keep_on_after_hover_ms to keyboard_backlight_keep_on_ms, as its use is no longer limited to systems where hover detection is supported.
